title: LGIC_NAMING round 2 -- the N5 layout briefing (LN-l-2's seat reads it; the addresses are round 1's N5_ADDRESSES.json and the key is round 1's N5_KEY.json, both unchanged)
issued_by: 2.0.0_SA_COO~G at the round-2 recut, under 1.0.0_SA_CTO's RULING K (round-1 analysis s.4 @de52d3db04): the briefing states what each slot holds under every tier, code included. Source: NAMING_SCHEMA.json v1.6, key block (grammar, scope_rule, tier, code, partition).
changed_from_round_1: the segment_roles scope line follows scope_rule at v1.6, and what_each_segment_holds_under_each_tier is new; the_layout and the three real examples are round 1's

briefing_layout.what_you_learned: How an address reads in the main shared bucket, opal-data-assets. Each address is s3://<bucket>/ followed by segments separated by '/'.

segment_roles.source: who the data comes from: a vendor feed, or for derived data the product or system that built it
segment_roles.scope: whose data it is: a firm; global when every firm shares it; a vendor master account; or, beneath a vendor feed, the product that feed serves
segment_roles.tier: the processing tier: bronze, silver, gold, platinum, state or code
segment_roles.table: the table name, except under tier code (see below)
segment_roles.partition: the partition: a date=YYYY-MM-DD, or an entity=id, or a named leaf

what_each_segment_holds_under_each_tier.bronze, silver, gold and platinum: table = the table name; partition = date=YYYY-MM-DD, or {entity}={id} (the key column's name and one id, for example advisor_id=A123), or a named leaf; object = the file under the partition
what_each_segment_holds_under_each_tier.state: table = the name of the state being kept; partition = a named leaf (for example latest); object = the file under the partition
what_each_segment_holds_under_each_tier.code: tier = code, a pipeline's code home beside its data; table = the TIER the code builds (bronze, silver or gold), so a tier word stands in the table slot; partition = the code file or bundle itself, as a named leaf; there is no object, so the address ends at the partition

briefing_layout.vintage: the three examples were listed live from opal-data-assets by 2.0.0_SA_COO~G on 2026-09-14 (s3api list-objects-v2, read-only)
